info.text: Interactive check questions for Lesson 10.2: Collaborative Peer Review, Schema Validation Sweeps, and CI/CD.

name.text: 01 Question: The Quality Assurance Gate in Textual Scholarship

questiontext.text: What is the fundamental principle of the dual-gate quality assurance architecture in digital textual scholarship?

generalfeedback.text: A robust digital edition relies on a dual-gate quality assurance architecture combining automated schema validation with structured human peer review.

answer.text: A robust digital edition relies on a dual-gate quality assurance architecture combining automated schema validation with structured human peer review.

feedback.text: Correct. Machines efficiently verify syntax, grammar, and Schematron constraints, freeing human scholars to focus on paleographical judgment and interpretive nuance.

answer.text: Requiring two different commercial software companies to certify the XML files before publication.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Quality assurance is scholarly and open-source, not dependent on commercial certification.

answer.text: Performing automated machine translation twice to verify linguistic accuracy.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Automated gates validate XML structure and rules, not machine translations.

answer.text: Eliminating human peer review in favor of automated algorithmic scoring.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Automated validation and human peer review are complementary gates; neither replaces the other.

name.text: 02 Question: The Fragility of Local Desktop Validation

questiontext.text: Why is relying exclusively on local desktop IDE validation (such as in Oxygen or VS Code) insufficient for collaborative digital editions?

generalfeedback.text: Local desktop validation is necessary for interactive authoring but insufficient for collaborative integrity, necessitating centralized automated validation gates.

answer.text: Local desktop validation is necessary for interactive authoring but insufficient for collaborative integrity, necessitating centralized automated validation gates.

feedback.text: Correct. Individual desktop setups often drift in schema versions or catalog paths, and editors may forget manual checks; centralized CI guarantees uniform, automated enforcement.

answer.text: Desktop IDEs are incapable of reading XML files larger than 10 kilobytes.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Desktop IDEs handle large files easily; the vulnerability is human inconsistency and local configuration drift.

answer.text: Local validation permanently locks the user's hard drive whenever a schema error occurs.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Local IDEs report errors visually with squiggly lines without locking hardware.

answer.text: Local IDE validation cannot check XML well-formedness.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Desktop IDEs check well-formedness, but relying on manual triggers permits unvetted commits.

name.text: 03 Question: The Multi-Tiered Validation Hierarchy

questiontext.text: What are the three distinct tiers of the multi-tiered XML validation hierarchy in digital scholarly editing?

generalfeedback.text: Comprehensive XML quality control operates across three distinct tiers: syntactic well-formedness, grammatical structure, and rule-based semantic constraints.

answer.text: Comprehensive XML quality control operates across three distinct tiers: syntactic well-formedness, grammatical structure, and rule-based semantic constraints.

feedback.text: Correct. Quality control progresses from basic syntactic well-formedness (W3C), through structural tree grammar (RELAX NG), to context-dependent semantic and relational business rules (ISO Schematron).

answer.text: Tier 1 ASCII encoding, Tier 2 HTML formatting, and Tier 3 PDF rendering.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The tiers govern XML data validation, not generic document rendering formats.

answer.text: Tier 1 Spell checking, Tier 2 Grammar translation, and Tier 3 Print layout.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The three tiers evaluate formal XML syntax, structural schemas, and semantic rule constraints.

answer.text: Tier 1 Git commit, Tier 2 GitHub push, and Tier 3 Zenodo archiving.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Those are version-control stages, not XML validation tiers.

name.text: 04 Question: Tier 1 Validation: XML Well-Formedness and Parser Mechanics

questiontext.text: Why do XML parsers enforce a strict fatal error policy upon encountering a syntax error, unlike web browsers rendering HTML?

generalfeedback.text: Well-formedness is the non-negotiable syntactic baseline of all XML, ensuring that documents can be parsed into unambiguous hierarchical trees.

answer.text: Well-formedness is the non-negotiable syntactic baseline of all XML, ensuring that documents can be parsed into unambiguous hierarchical trees.

feedback.text: Correct. Unlike HTML browsers which guess user intent through lenient error recovery, XML parsers mandate strict well-formedness to ensure deterministic tree parsing.

answer.text: XML parsers operate on low-power hardware that cannot execute error-recovery routines.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The fatal error policy is a deliberate W3C architectural standard to preserve structural precision, not a hardware limitation.

answer.text: Syntax errors in XML permanently corrupt the host operating system's file system.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Parsers simply halt execution and return an error code; no file system corruption occurs.

answer.text: HTML is a compiled binary format whereas XML is an interpreted plain-text format.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Both HTML and XML are text-based markup languages, but XML enforces strict tree grammar.

name.text: 05 Question: Tier 2 Validation: Grammar-Based Schemas with RELAX NG

questiontext.text: Why has the international digital humanities community standardized on RELAX NG rather than W3C XML Schema (XSD) for structural validation?

generalfeedback.text: RELAX NG enforces the geometric and structural grammar of TEI documents, verifying that elements nest according to established schema definitions.

answer.text: RELAX NG enforces the geometric and structural grammar of TEI documents, verifying that elements nest according to established schema definitions.

feedback.text: Correct. RELAX NG patterns cleanly express the complex, non-deterministic mixed-content structures of manuscript documents, whereas XSD imposes rigid object data-typing constraints.

answer.text: RELAX NG is the only schema language that supports non-English character encodings like Greek.

feedback.text: Incorrect. All modern XML schema languages support Unicode; RELAX NG is preferred for its expressive pattern-based grammar.

answer.text: W3C XML Schema (XSD) was deprecated and removed from the XML standard in 2010.

feedback.text: Incorrect. XSD remains widely used in commercial enterprise settings, but is poorly suited to humanistic texts.

answer.text: RELAX NG schemas compile directly into C++ binaries to accelerate web page loading.

feedback.text: Incorrect. RELAX NG validates XML document structure; it is not a web compilation language.

name.text: 06 Question: The Limits of Grammar: The OHCO Model and Business Logic

questiontext.text: What fundamental theoretical limitation prevents grammar-based schemas (like RELAX NG) from enforcing all philological rules in a TEI edition?

generalfeedback.text: Grammar-based schemas define structural shapes but cannot enforce conditional co-occurrence rules or cross-referential integrity across document trees.

answer.text: Grammar-based schemas define structural shapes but cannot enforce conditional co-occurrence rules or cross-referential integrity across document trees.

feedback.text: Correct. Under the OHCO model, grammar schemas evaluate context-free parent-child nesting but cannot evaluate dynamic cross-referential constraints, such as verifying that an apparatus pointer targets a declared witness ID.

answer.text: The OHCO model only applies to relational databases and cannot represent XML trees.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The OHCO model (Ordered Hierarchy of Content Objects) is the foundational data model of XML itself.

answer.text: RELAX NG schemas cannot read XML files containing more than three levels of nested tags.

feedback.text: Incorrect. RELAX NG handles arbitrary nesting depths; its limitation is context-dependent business logic.

answer.text: Grammar schemas cannot validate documents written in Unicode Greek.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Grammar schemas validate any Unicode text; their limit is cross-element relational logic.

name.text: 07 Question: Tier 3 Validation: ISO Schematron (ISO/IEC 19757-3)

questiontext.text: How does ISO Schematron differ fundamentally from grammar-based schema languages like RELAX NG?

generalfeedback.text: ISO Schematron uses XPath queries to validate complex business rules and conditional constraints that lie beyond the reach of grammar-based schemas.

answer.text: ISO Schematron uses XPath queries to validate complex business rules and conditional constraints that lie beyond the reach of grammar-based schemas.

feedback.text: Correct. Instead of defining an entire document grammar, Schematron evaluates targeted XPath boolean rules and returns actionable, human-readable diagnostic explanations.

answer.text: Schematron validates only file names and directory structures rather than document contents.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Schematron queries deep XML tree nodes and attribute values using XPath.

answer.text: Schematron is an interactive graphic drawing tool used to design manuscript page layouts.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Schematron is a formal XML validation standard based on XPath assertions.

answer.text: Schematron replaces XML with JSON data structures to simplify web publishing.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Schematron operates natively on XML trees and is standardized as ISO/IEC 19757-3.

name.text: 08 Question: Authoring Schematron Rules for Scholarly Editions

questiontext.text: In an ISO Schematron rule, what is the functional relationship between the sch:rule context and sch:assert test elements?

generalfeedback.text: Schematron rules combine XPath context matching with explicit boolean tests to generate tailored, actionable diagnostic feedback for editors.

answer.text: Schematron rules combine XPath context matching with explicit boolean tests to generate tailored, actionable diagnostic feedback for editors.

feedback.text: Correct. The context attribute matches focal nodes in the XML tree, while the assert test evaluates a boolean condition on those nodes, emitting a tailored diagnostic message if false.

answer.text: context defines the file path on disk, while assert test installs the required Java runtime.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Both are XML elements that evaluate in-memory Document Object Model nodes using XPath.

answer.text: context specifies the student's name, while assert test calculates their assignment grade.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Schematron evaluates document markup constraints, not student grading metadata.

answer.text: context is evaluated only if the assert test fails.

feedback.text: Incorrect. context matches the focal nodes first; then assert test is evaluated for each matched node.

name.text: 09 Question: Enforcing Cross-Reference and Identifier Integrity

questiontext.text: How does Schematron prevent dangling pointers (such as undeclared manuscript sigla in @wit attributes)?

generalfeedback.text: Schematron XPath assertions guarantee relational integrity by verifying that every internal pointer and witness siglum resolves to a valid declared identifier.

answer.text: Schematron XPath assertions guarantee relational integrity by verifying that every internal pointer and witness siglum resolves to a valid declared identifier.

feedback.text: Correct. Using XPath expressions like every $w in tokenize(@wit, '\s+') satisfies substring($w, 2) = //tei:witness/@xml:id, Schematron verifies that all witness references exist.

answer.text: It automatically deletes any rdg element that contains an unrecognized witness siglum.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Schematron alerts editors to invalid pointers via validation errors; it does not silently delete data.

answer.text: It queries the library's physical catalog database via an online API during parsing.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Schematron verifies relational integrity against identifiers declared within the TEI document.

answer.text: It restricts all apparatus entries to exactly one manuscript witness per reading.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Schematron supports multi-valued witness lists while ensuring every referenced ID is declared.

name.text: 10 Question: Validating Linguistic and Attribute Co-Occurrences

questiontext.text: What editorial constraint does Schematron enforce on TEI choice containers in normalization and correction layers?

generalfeedback.text: Rule-based validation prevents invalid editorial combinations, ensuring that normalization pairs and morphological tags conform strictly to project policy.

answer.text: Rule-based validation prevents invalid editorial combinations, ensuring that normalization pairs and morphological tags conform strictly to project policy.

feedback.text: Correct. Schematron evaluates boolean logic to ensure editors do not mix historical spelling regularization (/) with scribal error emendation (/).

answer.text: It mandates that every choice element must contain at least five competing readings.

feedback.text: Incorrect. choice typically contains two complementary views of a single reading (diplomatic vs. editorial).

answer.text: It requires that all reg readings be written in modern English rather than Greek.

feedback.text: Incorrect. reg contains the normalized Greek orthography matching standard lexicons.

answer.text: It forces editors to delete the original scribal spelling from the digital edition.

feedback.text: Incorrect. TEI preservation retains both the diplomatic orig and normalized reg readings.

name.text: 11 Question: Compiling and Executing Schematron via XSLT Engines

questiontext.text: How does the reference implementation of ISO Schematron execute validation against TEI XML files?

generalfeedback.text: Schematron operates by compiling XPath rules into XSLT stylesheets via Saxon, generating machine-readable SVRL reports of all constraint violations.

answer.text: Schematron operates by compiling XPath rules into XSLT stylesheets via Saxon, generating machine-readable SVRL reports of all constraint violations.

feedback.text: Correct. Schematron uses multi-stage XSLT transformations to generate a validator stylesheet, producing a Schematron Validation Report Language (SVRL) XML report of failures.

answer.text: It converts XML files into binary byte-code executed directly on the CPU.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Schematron is an XSLT-based pipeline processing XML trees into SVRL reports.

answer.text: It uploads documents to a commercial cloud server for proprietary parsing.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Schematron runs locally and in open CI containers using open-source XSLT processors like Saxon.

answer.text: It requires compiling a bespoke C++ compiler for each individual rule.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Standard Saxon XSLT engines execute the compiled Schematron stylesheets without C++ compilation.

name.text: 12 Question: Introduction to Continuous Integration (CI/CD) for Digital Humanities

questiontext.text: What is the primary methodological benefit of shifting left through Continuous Integration in digital scholarly editing?

generalfeedback.text: Continuous Integration automates quality control, running reproducible validation suites on every commit to prevent malformed data from entering canonical repositories.

answer.text: Continuous Integration automates quality control, running reproducible validation suites on every commit to prevent malformed data from entering canonical repositories.

feedback.text: Correct. Continuous Integration validates data automatically within seconds of pushing, catching defects at the earliest possible stage rather than during stressful post-production cleanups.

answer.text: Automatically publishing unedited manuscript transcriptions to commercial book distributors.

feedback.text: Incorrect. CI validates and protects data integrity; publication occurs only after formal approval.

answer.text: Eliminating the need for students to learn TEI XML markup rules.

feedback.text: Incorrect. CI reinforces learning by providing instant, objective feedback on XML conformance.

answer.text: Moving all project files from GitHub to proprietary offline servers.

feedback.text: Incorrect. CI runs on automated cloud runners connected to version-controlled repositories.

name.text: 13 Question: Anatomy of a GitHub Actions Workflow

questiontext.text: What are the essential building blocks that define a GitHub Actions workflow YAML file?

generalfeedback.text: GitHub Actions workflows define automated event-driven pipelines that execute validation tasks inside isolated, ephemeral virtual machines.

answer.text: GitHub Actions workflows define automated event-driven pipelines that execute validation tasks inside isolated, ephemeral virtual machines.

feedback.text: Correct. A declarative GitHub Actions YAML file defines workflow names, trigger events (push/PR), jobs, runner environments (ubuntu-latest), and sequential execution steps.

answer.text: <teiHeader>, <fileDesc>, <sourceDesc>, and <body>.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Those are TEI XML elements, not GitHub Actions YAML workflow directives.

answer.text: Classes, Objects, Methods, Inheritance, and Polymorphism.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Those are object-oriented programming concepts, not CI workflow configuration keys.

answer.text: Input, Output, Buffer, Cache, and Swap Space.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Those are low-level operating system terms, not CI pipeline components.

name.text: 14 Question: Writing a Complete TEI Validation Workflow

questiontext.text: In a complete TEI validation workflow on GitHub Actions, in what order should automated test steps be executed?

generalfeedback.text: A standard TEI validation workflow automates Java runtime provisioning, schema downloading, and multi-tiered validation across all repository XML files.

answer.text: A standard TEI validation workflow automates Java runtime provisioning, schema downloading, and multi-tiered validation across all repository XML files.

feedback.text: Correct. Testing follows the validation hierarchy: basic syntax is verified first with xmllint, followed by structural grammar with Jing, and finally complex semantic rules with Saxon Schematron.

answer.text: Execute Tier 3 Schematron rules before checking if the XML document is well-formed.

feedback.text: Incorrect. If a document is not well-formed, Schematron and RELAX NG parsers crash immediately on syntax errors.

answer.text: Compile the final PDF book before verifying whether the XML files contain syntax errors.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Validation must succeed before derivative publishing artifacts can be compiled safely.

answer.text: Deploy the website to the public server before running any automated validation steps.

feedback.text: Incorrect. CI pipelines act as gatekeepers; invalid commits must be blocked from deployment.

name.text: 15 Question: Integrating Community Validation Actions

questiontext.text: What is the main advantage of using community actions like adunning/xml-model-validator in a TEI CI workflow?

generalfeedback.text: Community-developed GitHub Actions streamline CI setup by automatically discovering XML-model processing instructions and executing standardized validation pipelines.

answer.text: Community-developed GitHub Actions streamline CI setup by automatically discovering XML-model processing instructions and executing standardized validation pipelines.

feedback.text: Correct. xml-model-validator parses processing instructions in each XML file to download and execute the exact RELAX NG and Schematron schemas specified by the document.

answer.text: It automatically translates English commentary into ancient Greek and Latin.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The action validates XML schemas; it does not translate prose.

answer.text: It permanently deletes any file that fails validation from the user's hard drive.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The action reports validation failures to the CI interface without destroying local files.

answer.text: It bypasses Java runtime requirements by converting TEI XML into Python scripts.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The action provisions Jing and Saxon under the hood to execute standard validation.

name.text: 16 Question: Associating Documents and Schemas: xml-model

questiontext.text: Why does the TEI standard recommend xml-model processing instructions rather than older DOCTYPE or xsi:schemaLocation declarations?

generalfeedback.text: Standard `` processing instructions declare the exact grammar and Schematron schemas governing a document, enabling both IDEs and CI runners to validate automatically.

answer.text: Standard xml-model processing instructions declare the exact grammar and Schematron schemas governing a document, enabling both IDEs and CI runners to validate automatically.

feedback.text: Correct. xml-model supports linking both structural grammar schemas and rule-based Schematron schemas simultaneously in a single standardized header.

answer.text: It encrypts the XML document so that only registered researchers can read the text.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Processing instructions are plain-text declarations intended for open interoperability.

answer.text: DOCTYPE declarations are illegal in XML and cause all modern parsers to crash.

feedback.text: Incorrect. DTDs are legal XML syntax, but cannot link Schematron schemas or support modern mixed content cleanly.

answer.text: xml-model automatically translates TEI documents into HTML without XSLT.

feedback.text: Incorrect. It associates validation schemas with the document; presentation transformations require separate stylesheets.

name.text: 17 Question: Converting CI Failures to Inline GitHub Annotations

questiontext.text: How do workflow commands like ::error file=...,line=...,col=... improve the pedagogical value of automated CI validation?

generalfeedback.text: Translating automated validation failures into inline GitHub annotations provides contextual, non-judgmental feedback directly alongside the offending markup.

answer.text: Translating automated validation failures into inline GitHub annotations provides contextual, non-judgmental feedback directly alongside the offending markup.

feedback.text: Correct. Translating raw CLI logs into inline diff annotations allows students to see exactly where and why their markup failed without searching through long build logs.

answer.text: They automatically penalize student grades by deducting points for every syntax error.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Annotations provide formative, non-judgmental feedback to help students learn and iterate.

answer.text: They prevent contributors from viewing other students' pull requests.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Annotations appear openly on the PR diff to facilitate collaborative learning and debugging.

answer.text: They lock the Git repository and require instructor intervention to unlock.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Authors simply push new commits to fix the highlighted errors.

name.text: 18 Question: Protecting Branches with Automated CI Merge Gates

questiontext.text: What is the function of GitHub Branch Protection Rules in a collaborative digital edition?

generalfeedback.text: Branch protection rules enforce automated merge gates, mathematically preventing malformed or unvalidated TEI data from polluting the canonical edition.

answer.text: Branch protection rules enforce automated merge gates, mathematically preventing malformed or unvalidated TEI data from polluting the canonical edition.

feedback.text: Correct. Branch protection ensures that unvalidated, failing, or unreviewed code cannot be merged into main, keeping the canonical corpus clean.

answer.text: They prevent unauthorized users from viewing public open-access repositories.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Branch protection governs write/merge permissions on specific branches, not public read visibility.

answer.text: They automatically delete any branch that has been inactive for more than twenty-four hours.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Stale branches are managed manually; branch protection protects production branches from bad merges.

answer.text: They enforce copyright restrictions by preventing readers from copying text.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Branch protection is a technical governance tool for repository branches.

name.text: 19 Question: Automated Preview and Artifact Compilation in CI

questiontext.text: Why should a digital edition CI/CD pipeline compile derivative formats (like HTML previews and PDF notes) during pull request evaluation?

generalfeedback.text: CI/CD pipelines can automatically generate static HTML previews and PDF reading notes, allowing reviewers to evaluate visual presentation alongside underlying code.

answer.text: CI/CD pipelines can automatically generate static HTML previews and PDF reading notes, allowing reviewers to evaluate visual presentation alongside underlying code.

feedback.text: Correct. Compiling derivative artifacts during CI allows reviewers to test dynamic tooltips, facsimile zooming, and apparatus layout before approving merges.

answer.text: Because TEI XML cannot be read or understood by human scholars in its raw text format.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Scholars read and write TEI XML directly; derivative previews verify presentation output.

answer.text: Because GitHub deletes raw XML files after every commit unless they are converted to PDF.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Git stores raw XML files permanently; artifact compilation generates optional preview files.

answer.text: To automatically publish the edition to commercial print bookstores on every push.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Artifacts attached to pull requests serve review purposes, not commercial publication.

name.text: 20 Question: The Boundary Between Automated Linting and Human Peer Review

questiontext.text: What essential editorial task lies strictly beyond the capability of automated CI validation and requires human peer review?

generalfeedback.text: Automated pipelines verify structural and syntactic conformance, liberating human peer reviewers to concentrate on interpretive nuance and philological rigor.

answer.text: Automated pipelines verify structural and syntactic conformance, liberating human peer reviewers to concentrate on interpretive nuance and philological rigor.

feedback.text: Correct. Automated pipelines verify syntax, grammar, and pointer resolution; only human scholars can evaluate paleographical evidence, semantic nuance, and editorial rationale.

answer.text: Verifying that all XML tags are closed and properly nested.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Automated parsers verify tag syntax and nesting instantaneously.

answer.text: Checking that witness pointers resolve to declared xml:id identifiers.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Schematron rules automate pointer and identifier integrity checks.

answer.text: Validating document conformance against RELAX NG schemas.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Jing and other schema validators automate structural grammar checking completely.

name.text: 21 Question: Designing a Structured TEI Peer-Review Rubric

questiontext.text: What are the six core domains evaluated in a comprehensive TEI digital scholarly peer-review rubric?

generalfeedback.text: A structured peer-review rubric provides an objective framework for evaluating both technical encoding standards and humanistic scholarship.

answer.text: A structured peer-review rubric provides an objective framework for evaluating both technical encoding standards and humanistic scholarship.

feedback.text: Correct. The rubric evaluates the complete lifecycle: Pipeline Validation, Structural Integrity, Philological Accuracy, Semantic Precision, Metadata Provenance, and Minimal Computing.

answer.text: Typography, Font Selection, Page Margins, Paper Weight, Binding Style, and Ink Color.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Those are physical print publishing specifications, not digital TEI peer-review domains.

answer.text: Grammar, Spelling, Punctuation, Word Count, Font Size, and Line Spacing.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Standard essay rubrics do not capture the technical and philological dimensions of digital editions.

answer.text: Download Speed, Server Uptime, Database Indexing, Network Latency, Bandwidth, and CPU Usage.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Those are system administration metrics, not scholarly TEI review criteria.

name.text: 22 Question: Auditing the teiHeader and Provenance Layer

questiontext.text: When auditing a peer's teiHeader, what is the purpose of inspecting the editorialDecl element?

generalfeedback.text: Auditing the `teiHeader` ensures that manuscript physical descriptions, provenance history, and contributor attribution meet international cataloguing standards.

answer.text: Auditing the teiHeader ensures that manuscript physical descriptions, provenance history, and contributor attribution meet international cataloguing standards.

feedback.text: Correct. The editorialDecl records the editorial principles and policies applied to the text, ensuring that future scholars understand how the critical text was established.

answer.text: To list the server passwords and administrator credentials for the repository.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The teiHeader contains bibliographic and scholarly metadata; credentials never belong in public markup.

answer.text: To store binary backups of all high-resolution IIIF manuscript images.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Facsimile metadata belongs in facsimile or external IIIF manifests.

answer.text: To record automated test results generated by continuous integration runners.

feedback.text: Incorrect. CI test results are reported in PR logs, not inside the teiHeader editorial declaration.

name.text: 23 Question: Auditing Diplomatic Transcription and Physical Milestones

questiontext.text: What must a peer reviewer verify when auditing physical milestone elements (pb and lb) against IIIF facsimiles?

generalfeedback.text: Auditing the diplomatic layer confirms that physical milestones and scribal alterations faithfully represent the primary manuscript evidence.

answer.text: Auditing the diplomatic layer confirms that physical milestones and scribal alterations faithfully represent the primary manuscript evidence.

feedback.text: Correct. Diplomatic milestones must represent physical codex structures faithfully, matching scribal page and line divisions visible in the IIIF facsimile.

answer.text: That line breaks occur exactly every ten words regardless of manuscript layout.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Line breaks must reflect the physical manuscript lines, not arbitrary word counts.

answer.text: That all page breaks are removed to create a continuous modern paragraph.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Diplomatic editions preserve original codicological divisions via pb milestones.

answer.text: That line breaks are encoded using HTML br tags rather than self-closing TEI lb elements.

feedback.text: Incorrect. TEI XML requires valid TEI elements (lb), not HTML markup.

name.text: 24 Question: Auditing Normalization, Collation, and Variant Apparatus

questiontext.text: When reviewing an apparatus criticus (app), what should a peer reviewer verify regarding the wit attributes?

generalfeedback.text: Auditing normalization and apparatus layers ensures that editorial emendations and variant readings are transparently documented and philologically justified.

answer.text: Auditing normalization and apparatus layers ensures that editorial emendations and variant readings are transparently documented and philologically justified.

feedback.text: Correct. Reviewers must cross-check that all @wit values point to declared manuscripts in listWit and that variant readings accurately reflect collation data.

answer.text: That every variant reading is translated into modern Latin and German.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Variant readings record the original manuscript text in its historical language.

answer.text: That only the reading preferred by the modern editor is included in the apparatus.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The apparatus criticus must record competing manuscript variants, not just the preferred reading.

answer.text: That wit attributes contain full URLs to online bookstore listings.

feedback.text: Incorrect. @wit contains private URI pointers to manuscript witnesses declared in the edition header.

name.text: 25 Question: Auditing Linguistic Markup and Morphosyntax (Assignment 3)

questiontext.text: When auditing a peer's linguistic markup on w tokens for Assignment 3, what common error in the @lemma attribute should reviewers flag?

generalfeedback.text: Auditing the linguistic layer verifies that Greek lemmas, morphological parsings, and grammatical attributes are philologically accurate across all encoded tokens.

answer.text: Auditing the linguistic layer verifies that Greek lemmas, morphological parsings, and grammatical attributes are philologically accurate across all encoded tokens.

feedback.text: Correct. The @lemma attribute must contain the clean, uninflected dictionary citation form (such as λόγος or εἰμί) without contextual enclitic accents or inflectional endings.

answer.text: Writing the Greek lemma in Unicode UTF-8 rather than Latin transliteration.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Lemmas in Greek editions must be written in proper Unicode Greek characters.

answer.text: Omitting the modern English translation from the @lemma attribute.

feedback.text: Incorrect. English glosses belong in translation or dictionary layers, not inside the @lemma citation headword.

answer.text: Using lowercase letters for Greek nouns.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Greek common nouns are properly lemmatized in standard lowercase.

name.text: 26 Question: Executing the In-Class Peer Review Exchange

questiontext.text: During the in-class peer review exchange, what is required when submitting formal review comments on a classmate's pull request?

generalfeedback.text: The peer review exchange provides real-world experience in evaluating, annotating, and adjudicating scholarly markup within an active collaborative repository.

answer.text: The peer review exchange provides real-world experience in evaluating, annotating, and adjudicating scholarly markup within an active collaborative repository.

feedback.text: Correct. Effective peer review requires granular, line-by-line feedback on specific markup decisions alongside a constructive summary evaluating overall schema and philological compliance.

answer.text: Clicking Approve immediately without reading the diff or checking CI status.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Uncritical approval undermines collaborative quality assurance and peer learning.

answer.text: Deleting the classmate's repository and rewriting the entire edition from scratch.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Peer review is an iterative dialogue providing constructive feedback to the author.

answer.text: Writing feedback in a private email rather than posting comments on the GitHub pull request.

feedback.text: Incorrect. All peer review must be recorded transparently on the pull request thread.

name.text: 27 Question: Case Study: The Digital Latin Library and the Traveling Imprimatur

questiontext.text: What is the concept of the Traveling Imprimatur pioneered by Samuel Huskey and the Digital Latin Library?

generalfeedback.text: The Digital Latin Library proves that version-controlled peer review can award authoritative academic credentials that travel independently of proprietary hosting platforms.

answer.text: The Digital Latin Library proves that version-controlled peer review can award authoritative academic credentials that travel independently of proprietary hosting platforms.

feedback.text: Correct. The Traveling Imprimatur separates peer-reviewed academic certification from commercial print platforms, awarding society-approved credentials to open, version-controlled TEI editions.

answer.text: A physical wax seal stamped onto printed parchment editions by European libraries.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The traveling imprimatur is a digital certification model for open-access repositories.

answer.text: An automated copyright enforcement algorithm that restricts access to Latin texts.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The model promotes open-access scholarly publishing under open licenses.

answer.text: A licensing fee paid by digital humanities projects to commercial software vendors.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The DLL model bypasses commercial gatekeeping in favor of society-governed open peer review.

name.text: 28 Question: Digital Longevity and the Endings Project Principles

questiontext.text: Which core architectural requirement from the Endings Project principles protects digital editions from software rot?

generalfeedback.text: Adhering to Endings Project principles ensures that digital critical editions remain functional, secure, and citeable for decades without ongoing server maintenance.

answer.text: Adhering to Endings Project principles ensures that digital critical editions remain functional, secure, and citeable for decades without ongoing server maintenance.
